problems: The figure reads as a long pin or matchstick, not clearly an awl. The bone grip is only about 50 px wide against a roughly 300 px shaft, so the handle is too small to read as a grip.

The handle outline is cramped. The crown (88657), right shoulder (88267), left shoulder (88886) and collar (88899) sit within about 50x65 px, so the shoulders and the narrowing into the shaft are hard to tell apart.
The blue thin outline around the handle looks like a traced ellipse rather than part of the silhouette, which makes the top read as a loop or ring.
Labels overlap the figure and each other: 'left shoulder' and 'collar' run across the gold lines and the handle, and 'right shoulder' and 'crown' are cut off at the frame edge.

Orientation is correct: handle at top, point at bottom (88765 at about y 470, the lowest point). The shaft is a straight, believable line from the collar down to the point, and the lower-shaft star 88771 sits just above the tip.
output.advice: Keep the orientation and the shaft. Redraw only the handle, which is the weak part. In the 555-px frame: (1) Widen the grip into a clear bulb about 2x its current width, roughly x 340–392 and y 100–165. (2) Place the crown 88657 at the top centre, about (366, 100). (3) Put the right shoulder 88267 at the outermost right swell, about (392, 128). (4) Put the left shoulder 88886 at the outermost left, about (341, 130), so the outline turns back inward there. (5) Put the collar 88899 where the bulb narrows into the shaft, about (360, 165). (6) Run one straight, slightly tapering shaft from the collar down to 88771 at about (371, 449), ending at the point 88765 at about (371, 472). (7) Remove the blue ellipse and draw only the single gold silhouette. (8) Move the labels to the open right or left margin with leader lines so they do not sit on the figure or cut off at the edge.
